prompt: Davi's first draft has six lines and every team lead found their wish in it. By the lesson, what is wrong with that?
hint: What does agreement tell you about choosing?

choices.text: The lines are too vague for any team to estimate or plan against
choices.why: Vagueness is one symptom, but a precise list of six wishes would still have chosen nothing.

choices.text: Nobody can disagree with it, so it has chosen nothing
choices.why: Right: choosing is the work a strategy does, and a document that upsets nobody has not done it.

choices.text: It has more lines than a page can hold
choices.why: Six lines fit easily. The number of lines is not what the lesson objects to.

choices.text: It was written by one engineer instead of by the CTO who owns the decision
choices.why: Who holds the pen does not matter here; the second draft has the same author and works.

prompt: Match each line of Davi's first draft to the hallmark of bad strategy it shows most clearly.
hint: Fluff has no mechanism; a goal has a target and no approach.

pairs.left: Be the most reliable ticketing platform in Brazil
Six goals for 52 engineers, several competing for the same people
Nowhere does it say what is going wrong

prompt: A team is handed "reach 99.99% availability" and nothing else. What does the lesson say happens next?
hint: A target with no approach.

choices.text: The team stops shipping features until the target is met
choices.why: Nothing in a bare target says to stop anything; that is exactly what it fails to say.

choices.text: Each team relabels work it already wanted
choices.why: Right: with a target and no approach, the goal becomes a label for whatever was planned anyway.

choices.text: The team asks for a diagnosis first
choices.why: That would be a healthy reaction, and it is not the one the lesson describes.

choices.text: Availability rises, because a number focuses effort
choices.why: A number can focus effort only when somebody has said how; here nobody has.

prompt: Why does the lesson call a list of goals "politically cheap"?
hint: Think about who loses an argument.

choices.text: It needs no budget approval
choices.why: Budget is not the cost meant; the cost is the argument nobody had to have.

choices.text: Executives prefer short documents
choices.why: A short document can still choose. Length is not the point here.

choices.text: Nobody loses an argument, so nobody has to be told their project waits
choices.why: Right: a real strategy produces losers on paper, and a list avoids that by choosing nothing.

choices.text: Each goal maps to one team, which keeps ownership clear
choices.why: One goal per team is how a list hides its conflicts, not a strength of it.

prompt: Put the three parts of Rumelt's kernel in the order each depends on the one before.
hint: You cannot choose an approach to a problem you have not named.
trap: Starting from actions is exactly the list of goals: steps with no stated problem behind them.

prompt: Which of these is a diagnosis in Rumelt's sense?
hint: Could somebody check it against data and find it false?

choices.text: Our architecture does not scale
choices.why: An opinion: nothing in it could be checked and found false.

choices.text: We will be the most reliable platform in the market
choices.why: That is fluff, and a goal; it says nothing about what is going on.

choices.text: Checkout fails in big on-sales, from one module every team edits
choices.why: Right: it names one challenge, ranks it, and the incident log could refute it.

choices.text: We have tech debt, slow tests, a big bill and old front-end code
choices.why: Every problem at once is the goal list with different verbs; a diagnosis picks one.

prompt: By the lesson, a guiding policy earns its place by what it ___.
hint: "Improve reliability" fails this test.

prompt: A strategy's actions read: "All teams are encouraged to consider reliability in their planning." Which row of the kernel test does it fail?
hint: Who does this, from when, instead of what?

choices.text: The diagnosis row, since it names no problem
choices.why: It may also lack a diagnosis, but the sentence quoted is an action, and it fails as one.

choices.text: The actions row: it commits nobody to anything
choices.why: Right: "all teams" and "encouraged" are the failing answers the table lists for actions.

choices.text: None: encouragement is a light form of guiding policy
choices.why: A policy rules things out; encouragement rules nothing out and commits nobody.

choices.text: The policy row, because reliability is too broad a theme for one team
choices.why: The breadth of the theme is not the failure; the absence of an owner and a date is.

prompt: Five initiatives, each excellent on its own, each taking a whole team. Why is that not yet a strategy?
hint: Coherent.

choices.text: Five is too many for any company
choices.why: The count is not the test; five actions that reinforce each other would be fine.

choices.text: They have no metrics attached
choices.why: Metrics help you know whether a strategy works; they do not make the actions coherent.

choices.text: Nothing ties them together, and they compete for the same people
choices.why: Right: coherent actions make each other work better; these only share a budget.

choices.text: Initiatives belong in a roadmap rather than in a strategy document
choices.why: Actions are a part of the kernel; the problem is these actions, not their presence.

prompt: What did Davi do differently before writing the second draft?
hint: What hurt, rather than what they wanted.

choices.text: Read incident reports and asked what hurt
choices.why: Right: the diagnosis came from evidence, not from collecting wishes.

choices.text: Asked the team leads to rank their own wishes
choices.why: Ranking wishes still starts from wishes; Davi started from what was failing.

choices.text: Benchmarked Coreto against the strategy documents of competitors in the market
choices.why: Another company's document cannot diagnose Coreto's problem.

choices.text: Cut the list down to its three cheapest goals
choices.why: A shorter list is still a list; cost was not how the second draft chose.

prompt: Which of these does Coreto's guiding policy rule out this year? Choose all that apply.
hint: Protect the on-sale first.

choices.text: Starting the microservices migration
choices.why: Yes: a company-wide migration would pull every team away from the one path that matters.

choices.text: Adopting the new front-end framework
choices.why: Yes: the framework waits, in the lesson's own words.

choices.text: Building a load test for the on-sale traffic
choices.why: That is one of the coherent actions, not something the policy excludes.

choices.text: A cloud-cost project that stays off the reservation path in the season
choices.why: The policy allows it on exactly that condition.

prompt: Davi removes the deploy freeze from the four actions. By the lesson's reasoning, what is the effect?
hint: Coherent actions: remove one and the others…

choices.text: None, because the load test already covers the risk
choices.why: The load test reduces the need for the freeze over time; while the debt work is under way, the freeze is what buys safety.

choices.text: The other three work worse
choices.why: Right: the freeze protects on-sales while the fix is under way, and the actions reinforce each other, which is what makes them a strategy and not a list.

choices.text: The policy turns into a list of goals
choices.why: The policy stays the same; what weakens is the set of actions carrying it out.

choices.text: The Reservations team loses its ownership of the module
choices.why: Ownership is a separate action and does not depend on the freeze.

prompt: What became of "reach 99.99% availability" in the second draft?
hint: Demoted from strategy to consequence.

choices.text: It became the guiding policy
choices.why: A target cannot be a policy: it says where, not how.

choices.text: It was deleted as fluff
choices.why: The line about being the most reliable platform was fluff; this one survived in another role.

choices.text: A way to know if the strategy works, measured on on-sale days
choices.why: Right: a goal kept as a measure of the strategy rather than as the strategy.

choices.text: It became one of the four coherent actions, owned by the Platform team
choices.why: The Platform team builds the load test; availability is how the result is judged.

prompt: Coreto counts an engineer-hour at R$ 150. What does one two-hour meeting of six engineers cost, in reais?
hint: People × hours × rate.

prompt: You typed =1+1 into a cell and the cell shows =1+1. What does the lesson say is going on?
hint: The cell's format.

choices.text: The spreadsheet is in another language
choices.why: A language mismatch breaks function names, and + is not a function name.

choices.text: The cell is formatted as text
choices.why: Right: a text cell stores what you typed instead of calculating it. Clear its formatting and type it again.

choices.text: Calculation has been switched off for this file
choices.why: That would leave an old value, not the formula itself on display.

choices.text: The installation failed
choices.why: A failed installation would not open at all; this one opened and stored text.

prompt: Which spreadsheet path does the course recommend, and what is the reason given that the other two do not share?
hint: No account, no connection, and the same numbers as the lessons.

choices.text: Google Sheets, because it needs nothing installed
choices.why: It needs nothing installed, but it does need an account and a connection, which is why it is the alternative.

choices.text: Excel, because it is what companies use
choices.why: Excel works and gives the same numbers, but it is paid, and the course does not recommend it.

choices.text: Calc in a virtual machine, since it keeps the course apart from your own files
choices.why: The virtual machine only pays off if you already live in one; it adds cost and no new number.

choices.text: Installed Calc: free, offline, and it computed the course's values
choices.why: Right: every value shown beside a formula is what LibreOffice 24.2 returned.

prompt: Match each symptom in the trouble sheet to its cause.
hint: One of them shows no error at all.

pairs.right: A function name from another language
A decimal comma in an English spreadsheet

pairs.left: A result a hundred times too large

prompt: One cell in a column of costs holds the text R$ 150. What happens to the total of that column?
hint: The error spreads.

choices.text: The total ignores that cell and is slightly low
choices.why: In the sheet the lesson built, the total did not skip the cell: it became an error.

choices.text: The total becomes #VALUE! as well
choices.why: Right: =SUM(D2:D3) returned #VALUE!, so one pasted cell took the summary down with it.

choices.text: The spreadsheet converts R$ 150 into 150 and the total is right
choices.why: The multiplication on that row already failed with #VALUE!, so nothing was converted.

choices.text: #NAME?
choices.why: #NAME? is an unknown function, not a text value.

prompt: A switching cost of R$ 210,000 is multiplied by a cell holding 10 instead of 10%. How many times too large is the result?
hint: Compare 2100000 with 21000.

prompt: A new head of engineering writes: "Our strategy: move fast, keep quality high, invest in people." Which hallmark of bad strategy fits it best?
hint: Would it read the same at any company?

choices.text: Bad strategic objectives, because three is too many
choices.why: Three is not too many by itself; the trouble is that none of the three says anything specific.

choices.text: Fluff: it says nothing specific
choices.why: Right: it sounds like insight, has no mechanism, and could be pasted into any company's slides.

choices.text: None: values like these are a valid guiding policy
choices.why: A policy rules something out; none of these three rules anything out.

choices.text: Failure to face the challenge, and nothing else
choices.why: It does fail to name a challenge, but the most visible fault is that the words carry nothing.

prompt: A company's diagnosis says: "Our mobile app's crash rate doubled after we moved to a cross-platform framework." Which guiding policy follows from it best?
hint: A direction that rules something out, tied to this diagnosis.

choices.text: Mobile stability first, features after
choices.why: Right: it responds to the diagnosis and says what loses when stability and features compete, until crashes are back to the old level.

choices.text: Become the best-rated app in our category within a year
choices.why: A goal, and fluff; it does not say how and excludes nothing.

choices.text: Hire two more mobile engineers to clear the bug queue
choices.why: That is an action, and without a policy nobody can say whether it is the right one.

choices.text: Improve quality across every platform we ship to
choices.why: It excludes nothing, so it guides nothing.

prompt: Rumelt calls the three parts a strategy cannot do without its ___.
hint: The centre of a seed.

prompt: Two team leads were upset by Coreto's second draft. How does the lesson read that?
hint: A document that chooses.

choices.text: As a sign the draft needs another round of consultation
choices.why: Another round to remove the upset would bring the list back.

choices.text: As a failure of communication by Davi
choices.why: The lesson does not blame the delivery; their projects really do wait a year.

choices.text: As the price of choosing
choices.why: Right: a document that chooses produces losers on paper, and the first draft upset nobody because it chose nothing.

choices.text: As proof the diagnosis was wrong about which problem matters most
choices.why: Disagreement is not evidence against a diagnosis; the incident log is.
